en: The zigzag path of Kennon Road acts as an inclined plane, reducing the effort needed for vehicles to climb the steep mountains of Benguet.
The sharp, pointed leaves of a pineapple plant act as wedges to protect the fruit and channel rainwater into the center.
The rough, fibrous texture of a dried coconut husk increases friction, making it an effective natural scrubber for cleaning sticky pots.
Earth’s gravity pulls the water of Pagsanjan Falls downward, creating a powerful, continuous cascade over the steep rocky cliffs.
The dark volcanic sand found in the beaches of Ilocos contains magnetite, a naturally magnetic mineral that sticks to magnets.
During a thunderstorm, lightning occurs when massive amounts of static electricity suddenly jump between negatively and positively charged clouds.
A rainbow appears over Baguio City after a rain shower because water droplets in the air refract and separate sunlight into different colors.
Shouting inside the Puerto Princesa Underground River creates a loud echo because sound waves bounce off the hard limestone cave walls.
Geothermal power plants in Tiwi, Albay, harness underground thermal energy from magma to boil water and produce steam for electricity.
The fast-flowing water of the Agus River possesses kinetic energy, which spins the turbines at the Maria Cristina Falls hydroelectric plant.
The gravitational pull of the moon causes the ocean water in Manila Bay to bulge outward, creating predictable daily high tides.
White sand on Boracay Beach reflects most of the sun's light and heat energy, keeping the shoreline cooler than dark volcanic sand.
